newsitem.title: USA: Cigarette makers propose $250,000 claim limit - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Cigarette makers propose $250,000 claim limit - WSJ.

text.p: In tobacco settlement talks, cigarette manufacturers have proposed setting firm limits for smokers looking for industry compensation, banning punitive damages and capping claims at $250,000, the Wall Street Journal said in its electronic edition on Wednesday.

The New York Times reported on Wednesday state attorney generals rejected proposals which would prevent smokers from bringing product liability claims against cigarette makers and limit them to suing tobacco firms for fraud.
According to people involved in the negotiations, the plan was likely to be rejected, the Journal said.

The Times said the industry proposal also sought to limit invidividual damage awards, punitive damages and legal fees, according to people familiar with the plan. The proposal would also cap the annual and total amounts of money cigarette companies would pay out, the Times said.

The Journal also said a controversial proposal involved preventing smokers from receiving money from the industry settlement fund unless they first sued cigarette makers and proved they were fraudulently misled by industry statements.
Richard Blumenthal, Connecticut attorney general who is participating in talks, was quoted in the Journal as saying: "I wouldn't put the chances of settlement above 50-50."
Philip Morris and RJ Reynolds were quoted by the Journal and the Times as declining to comment on talks.
